correctness.rationale: PASS: The generator identity (n+1)c=(n+2)a+5b and exact adjacent gcd(a,b)=(n+1)/gcd(n+1,6), gcd(b,c)=(n+2)/gcd(n+2,6) imply gcd(a,b,c)=1; also gcd(a,c)|5. For n>=3 all three generators minimal, using c<2a for n>=8 and checks n=3..7. The classical symmetric three-generator gluing criterion applies. For pair (a,b), a nonnegative representation of c after dividing by gcd forces t=0 in the 2-generated Diophantine general solution and hence gcd(n+1,6)=1; conversely it constructs gluing when n≡0,4 mod6. Pairs (b,c) and (a,c) are ruled out by divisibility and size inequalities. The gluing Frobenius formula yields [4n^5+32n^4+101n^3+175n²+102n−36]/36 and g=(F+1)/2. At n=1 S=N0, F=-1; at n=2 S=<5,14>, F=51. Independent Apéry shortest-path checks all 100 indices n<=100 agree, but all-n follows from gluing proof not enumeration.
